title: Receipt Export Envelopes
description: Deterministically re-expresses one caller-supplied execution receipt as two wire envelopes so lineage and eventing stacks can ingest estate receipts without a custom adapter. Envelope 1 is a lineage RunEvent: eventType COMPLETE, eventTime carried from the receipt, runId derived as a pure function of the first 16 bytes of the receipt execution_hash (version nibble 8, variant bits 10), job namespace/name from the receipt, one input dataset per parent hash named by hash in the estate lineage-card facet dialect, producer and schemaURL pinned to the vendored 1.55.0 schema. Envelope 2 is a structured-mode event envelope: specversion 1.0, id = the execution_hash, caller-declared source URI-reference, type co.ainumbers.ocg.receipt.v1, time = the receipt event time, datacontenttype application/json, data echoing the receipt fields unchanged. The receipt is caller-supplied and caller-asserted: the kernel never verifies the hash values, reads no clock, uses no randomness, performs no network access, and refuses (fail-closed, no envelopes emitted) any missing or malformed hash, timestamp or URI-reference. Scope limits: one receipt per call, no receipt-correctness verification, no timestamp assignment; a terminal export view that consumes nothing and feeds nothing.

receipt.description: One execution receipt: tool_id (non-empty string), execution_hash and policy_parameters_hash (64-character lowercase hex digests), parent_hashes (array of 64-hex digests) and parent_tool_ids (array of non-empty strings, same length as parent_hashes), chain_depth (non-negative integer), event_time (timestamp with date, time, optional fractional seconds and an offset), source (a well-formed URI-reference: printable US-ASCII, valid percent-escapes) and namespace (non-empty string). All members are required; any missing or malformed member is refused whole.
